text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The Economic Coordination Committee of the cabinet increased the support price of sugarcane by 10 rupees per 40 kg for 1997/98 (July-June) crop.
- Telephone communication between Karachi and the interior of Sindh was cut off from 5.0 p.m. on Tuesday, blocking all telephone and most fax calls.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub met U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright for 45 minutes, but no major breakthrough in talks over the stranded F-16 planes issue was reported.
- A local Pakistan Muslim League leader was shot dead in Karachi's Gulbahar area.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif confirmed that India was interested in buying 3,000 megawatts of electricity from Pakistan, said supplies were not sufficient for export now.

- South Korean multinational Hyundai Corporation has indicated it might initially invest $250 million in infrastructure projects including ports, power generation, telecommunications and developments of motorways in Pakistan.
- Pakistan's seafood exports to United States may face problems unless exporters and processors comply with the Hazard Analysis Critical Point, a U.S. inspection system.
- Outgoing Austrian trade commissioner Franz Schmirmaul said many companies are interested in joint ventures in Pakistan.
- Bankers Equity has halved the number of its employees in a major downsizing since its privatisation in June 1996.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Central Board of Revenue has notified reduction in duty drawback on carpet exports from 11.20 percent to 6.20 percent with effect from May 16.
- In a desperate move, the authorities have begun employing foreign experts in the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation on heavy remunerations to arrest its deterioration.
- On the advice of Asian Development Bank, the government will pump 200 million rupees into the National Investment Trust to improve its financial health before privatisation.
- The government and the labour unions are likely to strike a deal on how to lay off up to 200,000 banking sector employees.
THE NEWS
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told the Senate that an ESAF agreement with IMF will be signed in September.
- The revolt against General Abdul Rashid Dostum has not come as surprise for Pakistan, the foreign ministry said.
- The National Assembly adopted a resolution calling for interest-free loans to the agriculture sector
NATION
- The government will allocate 70 billion rupees for social sector development in the 1997/98 budget.
MUSLIM
- Benazir Bhutto has demanded that she be given the status of Opposition Leader in the National Assembly.
- The Election Commission will lodge a complaint with the prime minister against the Foreign Office for delaying the process to grant voting rights to overseas Pakistanis.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
